method: Hand-researched overlay. Legal and certification facts must cite an official sourceRef. Descriptive fields are deliberately conservative when a primary source has not yet been captured.

profiles.name: Champagne

terroir.climate: cool northern French climate with continental and oceanic influence

styleNotes: Pinot Noir contributes body and structure
Chardonnay contributes freshness and ageing capacity
Meunier contributes fruit and roundness
lees ageing develops autolytic and mature tertiary aromas
researchNotes: Chardonnay Rose returned to the authorized list in 2025 according to Comité Champagne.
The current legal file must remain versioned because Champagne specifications continue to be amended.

profiles.name: Chablis

terroir.geography: slopes around the Serein valley in northern Burgundy
terroir.soilResearchStatus: separate Chablis terroir source still to be added to provenance registry

styleNotes: dry, high-acid white wine
mineral and fresh profile
can gain aromatic complexity and finesse with age
researchNotes: INAO describes Chablis as capable of reaching plenitude around 8–10 years; treat this as a descriptive benchmark, not a hard drinking window.

profiles.name: Pauillac

terroir.climate: temperate oceanic, moderated by Atlantic and Gironde waters
soils: deep gravel mounds with varying sand content

styleNotes: structured and ageworthy
Cabernet Sauvignon commonly gives cassis, mint and cedar notes
Merlot adds rounder red and black fruit
Petit Verdot can contribute dark fruit and coffee-like notes
researchNotes: INAO states Pauillac contains 18 classified growths from the 1855 classification, including three first growths.
Full current 2026 specification still needs field-level extraction for maximum yield and analytical minima.

profiles.name: Barolo
styleNotes: high-structure Nebbiolo intended for substantial ageing
MGA and vineyard naming must be tied to legally delimited areas and naming rules
researchNotes: The 2026 consolidated specification explicitly covers Barolo, Riserva, MGA-labelled wines and conditional use of vigna plus a toponym.
The existing legacy project already contains extensive MGA material; this overlay should become the legal anchor for that hierarchy.

profiles.name: Chianti Classico
researchNotes: The 2023 specification makes the 90% Sangiovese / 10% named native-red rule for Gran Selezione effective from the fifth harvest after approval; until then compliant vineyards under the general 80/20 rule remain eligible.
Generation must therefore be vintage-aware when applying the Gran Selezione blend rule.

profiles.name: Brunello di Montalcino

productionRules.release: 1 January of the fifth year after harvest; Riserva one year later

styleNotes: dry, robust, harmonious Sangiovese
garnet development with age
suited to long ageing and structured food
researchNotes: Production is confined to the historic municipality of Montalcino.
A separate terroir-source pass will add the official 2025 geo-viticultural mapping rather than relying on generic north/south stereotypes.

profiles.name: Amarone della Valpolicella
products: dry red wine from dried grapes
styleNotes: dry, high-alcohol, concentrated red wine
grape drying increases concentration of sugars and polyphenols
long wood ageing supports extended bottle evolution
researchNotes: The full list and individual caps for additional permitted varieties must be extracted before blend generation is marked safe.

profiles.name: Franciacorta
styleNotes: fine persistent mousse
fresh and savory profile
bottle fermentation drives autolytic complexity

profiles.name: Rioja
researchNotes: Viñedo Singular rules are materially stricter than the generic DOCa yield rules and require a delimited, technically justified site.
Ageing categories differ for white/rosé and sparkling wines; generation must branch by color and product category.

profiles.name: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry

productionRules.dynamicAgeing: criaderas y solera used for many categories

styleNotes: biological ageing under flor defines Fino-family development
oxidative ageing defines Oloroso-family development
mixed biological and oxidative trajectories create intermediate styles
researchNotes: The current DOP specification is the authority for exact allowed varieties by wine type, fortification parameters, sugar categories and ageing terminology; those tables need a dedicated extraction pass.

profiles.name: Ribera del Duero
researchNotes: The official council reports a high-altitude vineyard range and substantial old-vine/bush-vine holdings; use these as regional distribution inputs, not universal bottle claims.
Full blend percentage rules need extraction from the current product specification before generation-safe status.

profiles.name: Priorat

terroir.slopeNotes: many vineyards exceed 15% slope; some sites approach 60%

researchNotes: The 'Noms de la Terra' hierarchy is a place-identity hierarchy with traceability controls, not merely an ageing hierarchy.
The council identifies 12 village growing zones and 459 named paratges in its classification project.

profiles.name: Vinho Verde
researchNotes: Subregional labels have their own permitted-grape subsets; the generator must not treat the general DO list as valid for every named subregion.
Certification also depends on yield, process, laboratory and sensory requirements.

profiles.name: Porto / Port
styleNotes: Ruby-family wines prioritize fruit preservation and reductive bottle development
Tawny-family wines are driven by extended oxidative wood maturation
Colheita is a single-harvest aged tawny style
Vintage and unfiltered LBV can continue developing substantially in bottle
researchNotes: Exact grape lists and beneficio/fortification parameters require a separate IVDP regulation extraction before bottle generation is marked safe.

profiles.name: Wachau DAC
researchNotes: Authorized varieties narrow as geographic precision increases: Riedenwein is limited to Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
Steinfeder/Federspiel/Smaragd coexist with DAC origin levels and should be modeled as a distinct traditional-style axis.

profiles.name: Kamptal DAC
styleNotes: Classic Grüner Veltliner emphasizes fresh fruit and fine spice
Classic Riesling emphasizes aromatic, mineral elegance
Reserve is denser and longer with subtle wood or botrytis notes permitted
researchNotes: A current Austrian legal-text pass should replace the older technical summary before hard-coding all modern origin tiers.

profiles.name: Barossa Valley
researchNotes: The GI was entered in the Register of Protected Names on 15 August 1997.
Legal identity and boundary are verified, but grape/style/soil claims need a separate Wine Australia regional research pass before this overlay changes generation behavior.

profiles.name: Marlborough
researchNotes: Boundary identity is verified by IPONZ. Grape and subregional style claims require separate regional evidence and should not be inferred from market reputation alone.

profiles.name: Central Otago
researchNotes: IPONZ recognizes Bannockburn as a GI wholly or partly within Central Otago; do not create unofficial nested subregions until individually researched.

profiles.name: Bannockburn
researchNotes: Bannockburn is formally registered and lies within the Central Otago GI. A later research pass should extract the applicant evidence on physical environment, soils, climate and reputation.

profiles.name: Martinborough
researchNotes: Legal GI identity is verified. Soil, climate, varietal distribution and style will be added only from the registered evidence or other authoritative regional material.

profiles.name: Wine of Origin framework
researchNotes: Geographical units, regions, districts and wards are legally distinct origin units. The generator must preserve their hierarchy rather than flatten every South African place to 'region'.
North West was added as a geographical unit in 2023 according to the 2025 national wine directory.

profiles.name: Chilean wine denomination-of-origin framework
researchNotes: The current Decreto 464 version is dated 14 July 2026 and should be treated as time-sensitive law.
Generation must model Chilean DO labels as percentage claims, not assume 100% origin/variety/vintage when a label names them.

profiles.name: Alto Agrelo
researchNotes: The INV formally recognized, protected and registered Alto Agrelo as an Argentine geographical indication in July 2025.
This pass intentionally records legal identity only; cultivar composition, elevations, soils and style require separate primary research.

profiles.name: Kakheti
styleNotes: traditional skin-contact/fermentation-with-must amber profile
fruit aromas with a firm, textural palate
researchNotes: Georgia's national wine body listed 30 registered PDO wine appellations as of April 2025; the research library should eventually model all of them individually.

profiles.name: Kindzmarauli
styleNotes: dark garnet color
full, velvety fruit profile
naturally semi-sweet

profiles.name: Akhasheni
styleNotes: dark pomegranate color
velvety sweetness
fruit-driven Saperavi profile
